About

Educator first. Builder always.

I'm Najia Elouaer, a Computer Science Educator with nearly two decades in the classroom, teaching programming, computational thinking, algorithms and digital technologies to the students who will build tomorrow's software — and, increasingly, tomorrow's AI.

Outside the classroom I stay a practitioner. I build with Flutter and Python, experiment with machine learning and prompt engineering, and keep close to the tools I ask my students to learn.

My teaching philosophy is simple: confidence first, code second. Before a student can debug a loop, they need to believe they're capable of understanding one. I design every lesson around that belief.

When I'm not teaching or coding, I'm usually somewhere with ruins, mountains, or a trail — traveling, hiking, photographing nature, and following the history under my feet.

Teaching Philosophy

Confidence first. Code second.

Four principles that shape every course, workshop and one-on-one I run.

01

Confidence First

Students learn faster once they stop fearing the terminal. I build psychological safety before syntax.

02

Logical Thinking

Code is applied logic. I teach students to decompose problems long before they touch a language.

03

Growth Mindset

Bugs aren't failures, they're data. I reframe every error message as a clue, not a verdict.

04

Student Success

The goal was never the grade. It's a student who keeps building long after the course ends.

Teaching Moments
"
The best lesson isn't the one students remember — it's the one that makes them believe they can figure out the next one alone.

My mentoring approach is hands-on and low-pressure: small wins early, real projects soon after, and permission to be confused without being stuck. I show up in the lab as often as I show up at the whiteboard — because a lot of learning happens in the space between the lesson and the deadline, when a student is quietly debugging on their own and just needs to know someone's around if they get stuck.
